title: Coixol ameliorates Toxoplasma gondii infection-induced lung injury by interfering with T. gondii HSP70/TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Shen, Xin-Yu; Lu, Jing-Mei; Lu, Yu-Nan; Jin, Guang-Nan; Ma, Jing-Wen; Wang, Jing-He; Wang, Yu; Xu, Xiang; Piao, Lian-Xun
one_liner_zh: 研究薏苡素通过干扰T.g.HSP70/TLR4/NF-kB信号通路改善弓形虫感染肺损伤，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Toxoplasma gondii (T. gondii) is an obligate intracellular protozoan parasite that causes pulmonary toxoplasmosis, although its pathogenesis is incompletely understood. There is no cure for toxoplasmosis. Coixol, a plant polyphenol extracted from coix seeds, has a variety of biological activities. However, the effects of coixol on T. gondii infection have not been clarified. In this study, we infected a mouse macrophage cell line (RAW 264.7) and BALB/c mice with the T. gondii RH strain to establish infection models in vitro and in vivo, respectively, to explore protective effects and potential mechanisms of coixol on lung injury caused by T. gondii infection. Anti-T. gondii effects and underlying anti-inflammatory mechanisms of coixol were investigated by real-time quantitative PCR, molecular docking, localized surface plasmon resonance, co-immunoprecipitation, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, western blotting, and immunofluorescence microscopy. The results show that coixol inhibits T. gondii loads and T. gondii-derived heat shock protein 70 (T.g.HSP70) expression. Moreover, coixol reduced inflammatory cell recruitment and infiltration, and ameliorated pathological lung injury induced by T. gondii infection. Coixol can directly bind T.g.HSP70 or Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) to disrupt their interaction. Coixol prevented overexpression of inducible nitric oxide synthase, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and high mobility group box 1 by inhibiting activation of the TLR4/nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB signaling pathway, consistent with effects of the TLR4 inhibitor CLI-095. These results indicate that coixol improves T. gondii infection-induced lung injury by interfering with T.g.HSP70-mediated TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling. Altogether, these findings suggest that coixol is a promising effective lead compound for the treatment of toxoplasmosis.
abstract_zh: 刚地弓形虫（Toxoplasma gondii, T. gondii）是一种专性胞内原虫寄生虫，可引起肺弓形虫病，但其发病机制尚未完全阐明。目前尚无治愈弓形虫病的方法。薏苡素（Coixol）是一种从薏苡仁中提取的植物多酚，具有多种生物活性。然而，薏苡素对弓形虫感染的作用尚未明确。在本研究中，我们分别用弓形虫RH株感染小鼠巨噬细胞系（RAW 264.7）和BALB/c小鼠，建立体外和体内感染模型，以探讨薏苡素对弓形虫感染所致肺损伤的保护作用及其潜在机制。通过实时定量PCR、分子对接、局域表面等离子体共振、免疫共沉淀、酶联免疫吸附测定、蛋白质印迹和免疫荧光显微镜技术，研究了薏苡素的抗弓形虫效应及其潜在的抗炎机制。结果表明，薏苡素抑制弓形虫载量和弓形虫来源的热休克蛋白70（T.g.HSP70）表达。此外，薏苡素减少了炎症细胞募集和浸润，并改善了弓形虫感染诱导的病理肺损伤。薏苡素可直接结合T.g.HSP70或Toll样受体4（TLR4），从而破坏它们的相互作用。薏苡素通过抑制TLR4/核因子（NF）-κB信号通路激活，阻止诱导型一氧化氮合酶、肿瘤坏死因子-α和高迁移率族蛋白B1的过表达，这与TLR4抑制剂CLI-095的作用一致。这些结果表明，薏苡素通过干扰T.g.HSP70介导的TLR4/NF-κB信号传导，改善弓形虫感染诱导的肺损伤。总之，这些发现提示薏苡素是治疗弓形虫病的一种有前景的有效先导化合物。
